ACT.when: after a model proposes a tool call

route.note: Abstract tiers. The host maps them onto whatever engines it runs. NO_MODEL means 'no generative call is needed to satisfy this turn' -- it is a routing tier, not an instruction to stay silent. The host still responds, from a canned acknowledgement, a template or a cache. A host that treats NO_MODEL as 'send nothing' will leave users staring at silence; see the model card on the confidence floor.

risk.note: Combine as max(deterministic_rules, encoder). The encoder may raise a tier and may never lower one. Encoder-alone P0 recall is 0.726 on the test pool.

gate.meaning: probability a human should confirm before the action runs

abstain.note: Present so the exported graph shape is final. The corpus carries no OOD labels, so this head was not trained and its output is meaningless. The shipped pipeline derives abstention from route-head entropy instead, which is an uncertainty signal and not OOD detection.

cost_matrix.note: Fixed before training. The training objective is expected cost under this matrix, so the minimised quantity and the reported metric are the same function.

input_handling.behaviour: truncation ceiling, not a padded width
input_handling.note: Every tokenizer call passes padding='longest', so a turn costs what its own length costs and the ceiling never widens a tensor. Raising it is free for short traffic. It was 64 in earlier revisions, which silently clipped the tail off long turns -- and the tail is where this corpus puts the clause that decides the tier, so a clipped turn was a mislabelled turn, not a degraded one.
input_handling.trained_length: No training example exceeds 47 tokens. The ceiling prevents truncation; it does not confer competence on long turns, which remain out of distribution.

model.int8.onnx.reason: Safety metrics identical to fp32 -- same P0 recall, same zero regret -- but routed 12.9% more expensively, breaching the 5% operational bound in the export gate. Not shipped, and not present in this distribution.
